title: Agent-gateway readiness: bind the state layer to managed agent runtimes in two phases, generic only
context: Managed agent runtimes (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and peers) run orchestrator + specialist agents behind an MCP gateway with identity, sandbox and telemetry, but leave the record open: non-deterministic paths, verdicts only in traces, policy by retrieval, escalations as dead ends. Hunch already holds the contract and rules (decisions with one live answer per topic, commitments, receipts, entities, idempotent refusals, replay). What is missing is reachability from such a runtime and what a regulated organization requires. A prospect's demo (AWS Summit Tel Aviv 2026, DEM304 fraud investigation) surfaced the gap list.
decision: Add a roadmap section 'Agent-gateway readiness' with two phases. Phase A (reachable from a managed runtime): MCP over streamable HTTP in `hunch serve` at POST /nuryel/v1/mcp through one dispatcher shared with the REST routes; a deployable container image plus one reference cloud deployment; the Python client on PyPI with agent-framework tool wrappers; a read-or-compute helper in the clients; a worked multi-agent sample under examples/ only. Phase B (acceptable to a regulated organization): subject-scoped erasure without giving up the git-native source of truth; OIDC/JWT via JWKS mapped to principals; OpenTelemetry/audit export; multi-instance serving with a measured throughput number; operator write actions in the shared state view. Every item is a generic binding or packaging of the existing contract; the only prospect-specific artifact is the sample and it never enters core. Each item flips only on named acceptance evidence.
consequences: hunch serve gains a second transport for the same verbs; the REST handler is refactored into a shared dispatcher so both transports cannot diverge.
New dependency surface: OIDC verification, OTel exporter and a container build enter the published artifact in Phase B.
Erasure forces a design choice about git history retention; it is the item most likely to gate a regulated deal and must be designed, not patched.
ROADMAP.md checkboxes flip only on the evidence named per item; no item is marked done on a claim.
alternatives_rejected: An AWS-specific adapter (Lambda wrapper, AgentCore SDK integration) inside Hunch — violates the single-integration-surface direction: orchestrators map their world to the contract, Hunch ships no adapters.
Building the fraud sample into the product as a domain feature — domain samples live in examples/; core stays domain-free.
Hosted Hunch as the answer to reachability — hosting stays deferred (non-goal) until an external partner asks; a container plus reference deployment is enough.
Putting Phase B before Phase A — nothing in B can be evaluated by a partner who cannot yet reach the server.
